frameworks.name: Sales Training Progressive Stages
frameworks.definition: A structured sales onboarding process that moves reps through game-tape study, half-load schedules, call review with Socratic questioning, and scripted drill-down to internalize messaging at the word level.

frameworks.name: Script Mastery via Repetition
frameworks.definition: Breaking down complex sales interactions into minute-level script components, drilling each component repeatedly until verbal delivery becomes subconscious, then moving to the next component.

claims.text: Any skill can be trained to mastery; the limiting variable is institutional investment in training resources, not the learner's inherent capability. Even individuals with severe cognitive constraints can achieve specialized mastery (neurosurgeon-level) given sufficient training design and repetition.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Skill must be decomposable into sub-skills
Institution must commit required training resources
claims.mechanism: Breaking down any skill into its sub-skill components and training each component separately, from the bottom up (elementary motor skills to complex decision-making), removes the constraint of 'innate ability' and makes mastery a function of cumulative training only.
bounded_by: Does not apply to constraints that are non-trainable (e.g., physical impossibilities or biological absolutes)
Timeline variability: some individuals may require multiples more hours than others

claims.text: Higher-skilled individuals require more detailed instructions, not fewer; as skill increases, the instruction becomes more granular rather than less. Vague directional mandates work only after an individual has already internalized all underlying sub-skills through prior training.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Applicable to complex multi-sub-skill domains (sales, business operations, execution)
Assumes prior training on foundational sub-skills
claims.mechanism: Skill depth increases problem-solving capacity. A high-skilled operator can take a vague mandate ('start a company around this'), map it to sub-skills they've already mastered ('content, sales, operations, ad management'), and execute autonomously. A novice hearing the same mandate fails because they lack the sub-skill inventory. Therefore, detailed instruction is load-bearing for early-stage learners; vague direction is only viable post-mastery.
bounded_by: Does not apply to rote tasks that are not multi-dimensional (data entry, assembly line work where instruction can remain granular indefinitely)

claims.text: Sales directors are operators first and sellers second; the binding role is running culture, training, and motivation, not personal close rate. An exceptional sales director is willing to repeat themselves over and over, play therapist to reps in cold streaks, and role-play until exhaustion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales teams at scale (40+ person range or larger)
High-touch service or consultative sales model
claims.mechanism: Culture and training consistency are the primary scalability levers in sales organizations, not individual rep quality. A director who personally models training standards, invests in repetition, and handles rep psychology compounds the entire team's performance. Personal sales success in a director is actually orthogonal to team success if personal selling crowds out training time.
bounded_by: Does not apply to solo-founder sales or single-rep operations where the founder must close personally
Does not apply to transactional/high-volume sales where rep training is minimal

claims.text: Script adherence is the primary operational control variable in sales training; if 100% of reps follow the script identically and conversion still fails, the script itself is the problem, not the rep. Adherence without results transfers accountability from rep to management.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales team structure with documented scripts and measurable compliance
High-touch discovery or solution-based sales (not transactional)
claims.mechanism: When script adherence is enforced, either two outcomes occur: (1) reps follow the script and close at X% rate, proving the script works, or (2) reps follow the script and close at 0%, proving the script fails. Before adherence, the outcome is ambiguous — was the rep lazy or does the script suck? Enforcing adherence removes rep variance from the equation, making the script itself the testable variable. This moves accountability from 'rep skill' to 'script quality.'
bounded_by: Does not apply to consultative/relationship-driven sales where conversation flow needs flexibility
Assumes scripts are actually well-designed (e.g., not obviously terrible)

claims.text: New sales reps should study 60-100 hours of recorded call footage (game tape) of top-performing reps before taking live calls, to internalize script patterns and decision-making at the subconscious level. This minimizes expensive early-stage rep failures and preserves lead quality.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-ticket sales where lead waste is expensive
claims.mechanism: Reps must internalize successful call patterns at the neural level ('subconscious') before executing live, because real-time decision-making under pressure exhausts cognitive load. Watching patterns repeatedly trains pattern recognition without the stress of live performance, lowering the cost of early failure.
bounded_by: Assumes footage is positive-exemplar only (not negative examples)
Assumes rep has completed foundational product/offer knowledge before game-tape phase

claims.text: New reps should take only 50% or 33% of scheduled calls in their first period, even if they could take a full load, to prevent single-day failure cascades that damage rep psychology. Controlled load preserves motivation and allows pair coaching with the sales director.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: New rep first 30-60 days of live calling
claims.mechanism: Overloading a new rep in their first live-call session creates cognitive overload and rapid failure accumulation, which triggers psychological shutdown ('I'm not cut out for this') and resignation. A controlled schedule (half or third load) ensures slower failure rate, giving coaching time between calls and preserving the rep's self-efficacy narrative.

numbers.axis: new-rep call load as percentage of full schedule

bounded_by: Does not apply to high-volume or transactional sales where reps expect high dial volume as baseline

claims.text: In post-call coaching, ask the rep 'What do you think you could have done better?' before offering your own critique. If the coach tells the rep the answer first, the rep internalizes it as criticism ('you suck') rather than self-discovery. Flipped questioning preserves psychological safety and improves retention.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Training relationship where psychological safety is a lever
claims.mechanism: When the coach delivers critique, the rep's brain activates shame and defensiveness, which shuts down learning ('I'm bad'). When the rep self-identifies the gap, the learning is owned, framed as growth rather than failure, and stored as 'I can improve this.' The coach's Socratic role (questioning rather than telling) preserves the rep's agency in the learning narrative.
bounded_by: Assumes the rep has sufficient self-awareness to identify real gaps
May require follow-up if rep's self-critique is inaccurate (coach then redirects gently)

claims.text: Team game-tape sessions (group call reviews) should include only positive commentary from peers; the rep provides their own critique, then the manager identifies the specific one-on-one gap. This preserves team psychological safety while directing coaching privately.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Team sales training / weekly group call reviews
claims.mechanism: Public critique from peers activates status anxiety and shame, reducing team trust and psychological safety. Public praise activates belonging. By reserving critiques for private one-on-ones, the team stays in 'we improve together' psychology, while the manager's private coaching delivers specific skill work without status loss.
bounded_by: Assumes manager has regular one-on-one time to deliver private coaching
Does not eliminate need for constructive feedback, just relocates it to private settings

claims.text: Drill script components at the atomic level (e.g., the five-second opening, the 'need more information' objection response) until the rep can deliver them verbatim from subconscious muscle memory. Move to the next component only after mastery, not in bulk.

Enforce script adherence as a non-negotiable employment standard. If a rep deviates, treat it as a culture violation ('He's a joker, get him out'), not a coaching opportunity. This makes the script the enforceable team norm.

Select salespeople based on whether they produce results and show progression, not on whether they try hard or are good people. Measure progression by booked meetings, contacts, and other activity metrics that predict results.

When evaluating a skill's trainability, assess the learner's prior related experience (building blocks) from other domains—e.g., sports experience teaches emotional resilience to rejection, reducing onboarding time. Map these building blocks onto the learning curve to set realistic expectations.

examples.text: When Alex Hormozi was named co-owner of a school, he gave the team one vague directive: 'Promote the school.' Instead of breaking it into sub-tasks ('send emails like this,' 'write hooks like this,' 'run ads like this'), he could execute directly because he had already mastered content marketing, sales, market positioning, and ad management from prior ventures. Each of these is a sub-skill he had trained independently.

A salesperson new to the role watches 60-100 hours of recorded calls from top-performing reps. During this phase, they study how the best reps handle specific moments: the opening, the needs-analysis questions, the objection response to 'I need more information.' They watch these moments repeatedly until they can mentally predict the next sentence.

In a post-call review, the manager pauses the recording and asks the rep, 'What do you think you could have done better?' The rep reflects and says, 'I was too soft on the close.' The manager then responds in the one-on-one, 'You need to work on rapport building' or 'You're struggling with the objection-handling part—let's drill that.' The rep self-identified the gap first; the manager then provides the specific skill-work direction.

During a weekly team game-tape session, the sales team reviews a call together. The rep watches their own call. A peer might say, 'You did really well on the discovery questions there.' The rep then self-critiques, 'I was soft on the close.' Then in the one-on-one with their manager, the manager addresses the close issue specifically and they drill it: 'When they say, oh, what\'s your main concern? Now we can go into it.' Repeated 5+ times until the rep\'s close language is automatized.

practices.text: Believe that you are worth the long-term investment in learning any skill, even if it takes you twice as long as others.
Focus post-call coaching on what the rep did well, not what they did wrong; let the rep self-identify gaps.
Train new reps on positive examples (what to do) rather than negative examples (what not to do).
Use game-tape review (recorded calls) as the most scalable and cost-effective training tool, to save expensive leads from early-stage rep errors.
Create a sales culture where team members police script adherence and hold each other accountable to the standard.
Make the one-on-one meetings serve a training function, not just a status check or motivation session.
